rules.statement: An OpenID Provider's discovery document must advertise only values the provider actually honours (response types, grant types, scopes, claims, auth methods, subject types, PKCE methods); add a value only together with the implementation that supports it.
rules.why: Conformance suites test everything advertised and fail or warn on anything the OP cannot honour, and clients rely on the metadata to choose behaviour.
rules.check: In a diff to discovery metadata or the settings behind it, look for a newly advertised value (e.g. an implicit/hybrid response type, an auth method, a claim) with no matching handler support, or a removed feature still advertised.

rules.statement: Advertise only asymmetric algorithms in `id_token_signing_alg_values_supported`, and make sure they match the signing keys published at the `jwks_uri`.
rules.why: Relying parties check ID tokens against the JWKS. An algorithm with no published key, or a symmetric one, fails validation.
rules.check: Look for symmetric (HS*) or `none` algorithms in the advertised ID token signing algorithms, or advertised algorithms that the keys served at the jwks endpoint don't cover.

rules.statement: Advertise and accept only `S256` as a PKCE code challenge method; never offer `plain`.
rules.why: The provider binds authorization codes to an S256 PKCE challenge, and `plain` is intentionally not offered.
rules.check: Look for `plain` added to `code_challenge_methods_supported` or accepted by authorize or token request validation.

rules.statement: The `issuer` in discovery metadata must exactly match (byte for byte) the public origin that clients use to reach the discovery endpoint, so derive it from the configured public origin and never hard-code a different host.
rules.why: Conformance suites and relying parties reject discovery when the issuer doesn't exactly match the discovery URL's origin.
rules.check: Look for issuer values built from a hard-coded host, or from a different host, scheme or port than the configured public origin, or that differ by a trailing slash.

rules.statement: Login and consent pages must keep stable element ids and names (username, password, login submit, consent allow and deny), and a change to any of them must update the browser-automation configs that reference them in the same change.
rules.why: Headless conformance automation finds elements by these selectors. If they drift, full automation breaks even when the protocol is correct.
rules.check: In a diff to login or consent markup, look for renamed or removed ids or names on form fields and buttons that don't come with a matching update to the automation config templates.

rules.statement: Never commit test-user passwords or client secrets in test or conformance config files: commit templates with placeholder tokens, fill them in at run time from per-machine generated credentials, and gitignore the rendered files.
rules.why: Each machine generates the conformance user's password outside the repository, and that password must never be committed.
rules.check: Look for literal passwords or secrets in committed config or template JSON, or for rendered config files that aren't gitignored.

rules.statement: Add an entry to a conformance expected-failures or expected-skips baseline only for a documented, intentional deviation, and give it a comment that links the issue or ADR that justifies it.
rules.why: The baseline keeps the gate green only for known non-support. Undocumented entries hide real regressions.
rules.check: In a diff to baseline files, look for new entries with no comment, or with a comment that links no issue or ADR.

rules.statement: Keep slow suites that need Docker or external services (such as external conformance harnesses) out of the fast, hermetic definition-of-done build script, and run them in a separate opt-in or nightly pipeline.
rules.why: The inner-loop build must stay fast and hermetic.
rules.check: Look for the main build or definition-of-done script gaining steps that start Docker, clone external repositories or need network services.

rules.statement: In Docker Compose files used for test infrastructure, pin each image to a specific release tag rather than `latest` or no tag.
rules.why: Pinned image tags keep test runs reproducible.
rules.check: Look for `image:` entries with no tag or with `:latest` in compose files.
